problem: Constraints-facing part only. C8 now says a guard that cannot decide denies and a recorder stays silent, and C12 puts every guarded path in the sandbox denyWrite. Two forks remain that only you can settle.

questions.text: How is Bash held to the locked and frozen paths?
questions.why: The sandbox is the mechanism the docs say cannot be talked past; a Bash PreToolUse hook parses commands and can be fooled. Both is belt and braces at the cost of a second mechanism to keep in step.

options.value: Sandbox denyWrite only, shipped active in project settings.
Sandbox plus a PreToolUse hook on Bash that denies commands naming a guarded path.

questions.text: Which phases carry an end-of-turn gate?
questions.why: v1 gated contracts and verify only; implement, where roles hold write access, had none. A gate in every writing phase is the constitution's floor; each gate needs a check to run.

options.value: Every phase in which a role can write: contracts, implement (per unit, the unit's own checks), verify (the acceptance check).
contracts and verify as today; implement is gated per unit by the worker's own frontmatter Stop hook instead of a global gate.

questions.text: When the stop gate reaches its eighth block and Claude Code overrides it, what does the run do?
questions.why: stderr on exit 0 reaches nobody. A stall must be visible to the session and must stop the run without the guards silently denying everything after.

options.value: The gate writes a halt into the run's record; the next SessionStart shows it as a systemMessage; every guard denies with a reason naming the halt; only a human clears it by editing the record.
The gate writes the halt and the run ends abandoned automatically, with the log entry stubbed.
